cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Judges are appointed by the King on the advice of the Prime Minister and Lord Chancellor — they must be independent

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: The principle of judicial independence means judges are free from political pressure and cannot be removed easily

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Judges are appointed through the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC) based on merit through open competition

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Magistrates are unpaid volunteers — around 12,000 sit in England and Wales, hearing 95% of criminal cases

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Magistrates must be aged 18-65 and have no serious criminal record — they receive training but no legal qualification is required

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Solicitors are legal professionals who advise clients, draft documents and can represent clients in all courts

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Barristers specialise in courtroom advocacy and providing specialist legal opinions — they are usually instructed through solicitors

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Juries of 12 ordinary citizens decide the verdict in Crown Court trials and some civil cases

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Legal executives are qualified legal professionals who specialise in a particular area of law

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) decides whether to prosecute criminal cases and presents cases in court

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Police officers investigate crimes, gather evidence and bring suspects before the courts

cards.front: Recall a key point about Legal Personnel
cards.back: Concerns exist about the diversity of the judiciary — it remains predominantly white, male and from privileged backgrounds

cards.back: 1. For Legal Personnel questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3.
